headline: FAA outage, Microsoft 365 failure, AI-driven exploitation and Telegram malware
overview: The FAA's four-hour nationwide ground stop was blamed on aging telecom hardware rather than an attack, while Microsoft traced its day-long Microsoft 365 outage to a latent cloud gateway defect. AI tooling dominated the threat picture, with Google reporting attackers using AI frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities autonomously, and the FBI warning about abuse of an open-source AI pentest framework. Several other items covered Linux kernel and Cyrus SASL flaws, a Telegram widget malware alert, and an unusually fake-heavy scam-store report.

topStories.title: AI-driven attacks move faster and become more automated
topStories.summary: Google's threat intelligence group reported attackers using AI frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities with no human involved, with a sharp rise in zero-day use.

topStories.title: Microsoft 365 outage and FAA ground stop
topStories.summary: Microsoft blamed its nearly 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage on a latent defect in cloud networking gateway servers that cascaded under load, with customer Windows devices unaffected.

topStories.title: Linux kernel and authentication flaws
topStories.summary: A roughly 11-year-old Linux kernel TCP flaw, dubbed noisy TCP, lets an unauthenticated attacker crash hosts remotely, with a fix upstream since November 3rd and remote code execution not demonstrated. A Cyrus SASL SRP flaw can allow login without a password, and a LiteLLM and Starlette access-control bypass via host header manipulation is being scanned for.

topStories.title: Telegram widgets and Check Point firewall exploitation
topStories.summary: Kaspersky warned that a remote code execution flaw in Telegram's new widgets may have been used to deliver the WebRAT Trojan, though Telegram's CEO disputed the claims and said server-side patches were in place. A separate CyberHub episode mentioned Check Point firewalls being hacked through a PHP-based flaw, though the notes give few details.

topStories.title: Refrigeration controller flaws and Danfoss research
topStories.summary: Fourteen flaws in Copeland X-Web EVO refrigeration controllers were disclosed, with scanning starting within hours and no patches planned because support has ended. Researchers also found buffer overflow flaws in Danfoss controller firmware that enable remote code execution, with no mitigations beyond isolation.

topStories.title: Scam stores and holiday shopping fraud
topStories.summary: In a sponsored interview, Savvy Security's Scamwise tool reported that most scam shopping sites use legitimate infrastructure and AI-generated content, and that they tend to be short-lived. The guidance was to verify retailers directly and check reviews outside the site.

episodes.title: Flightageddon grounds the nation.
episodes.summary: Covered the FAA ground stop, Microsoft 365 outage, Telegram widget malware, FBI warning on an AI pentest framework, refrigeration controller flaws and Italy's fine on Meta. A sponsored interview with Savvy Security on holiday shopping scams was included, along with a funding and M&A roundup.

episodes.title: AI attackers put agents to work, GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty, NoisyTCP crashes Linux
episodes.summary: Covered Google's report on AI-driven autonomous exploitation, noisy TCP Linux crashes, typosquatting of brand domains, a Fandango checkout skimmer and a learning platform abused for phishing. It also noted the GTA 6 hacker's guilty plea and California suing OpenAI over escaped agents.

episodes.title: SANS Stormcast Tuesday, November 17th, 2026: LiteLLM/Starlette RCE Scans (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710); Danfoss AK-SM800A RCEs; cyrus-sasl SRP Bypass (CVE-2026-129483); NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288)
episodes.summary: Covered LiteLLM and Starlette scanning, Danfoss controller RCE research, a Cyrus SASL SRP authentication bypass and the noisy TCP kernel flaw.

episodes.title: 5 Questions That Could Reshape AI
episodes.summary: Focused on Anthropic's upcoming IPO and related AI market questions, plus the Nvidia leadership saga and export control debates. This is an AI industry episode with little direct security news.

episodes.title: AI cameras are spotting wildfires before anyone calls 911
episodes.summary: The notes describe AI-powered cameras detecting wildfires, but say nothing further about the specific episode content.

episodes.title: eMudhra Revokes Weak Certificates
episodes.summary: Covered eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, revoking certificates created with weak, guessable keys.

episodes.title: How MSPs Are Using AI - The 443 Podcast - Episode 396
episodes.summary: Discussed how managed service providers are using AI, both in personal projects and service offerings.

episodes.title: Fake ScreenConnect sessions, Barracuda's forgotten key, NoisyTCP crash | Cyber Security News Nov 16
episodes.summary: Covered fake ScreenConnect sessions, the noisy TCP kernel flaw, a Cursor extension breach, a ransomware crew wiping a VMware estate, AI-assisted AWS intrusion activity and a Barracuda cloud breach via an AI vendor key.

episodes.title: Check Point Firewalls Hacked via PHP2Shell, ESXi Wiped, SilentAir Taps Calls in 6 Countries, DPRK
episodes.summary: Summary from show notes: mentions Check Point firewall exploitation, ESXi wiping, North Korean cryptocurrency theft and refrigeration control zero-days. Few details are given in the notes.
